security_scan.install_hint: brew install gitleaks | apt: see github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases

budgets._doc: Injection budgets in BYTES per point (EVOL-043). One reader measures the REAL producer at its worst case: python3 scripts/gate.py budget. Raising a key needs its record in the changelog. prompt_submit ≥ snapshot + the reload wrapper + the stale warning (the worst case forces both).

coherence._doc: Coherence gates (EVOL-044). certifying_artefacts: the verdict artefacts gate.py currency judges (terminal status/verdict must carry certifies: from gate.py certify). Empty list = a ratified opt-out.

surface._doc: Per-PR surface ceiling (EVOL-045). The reviewable unit is bounded per pull request: python3 scripts/gate.py surface measures files + lines of the diff vs the one diff base (gate.py diff-base) with no exclusion list; over a ceiling blocks the push unless a commit trailer `Surface-Escape: <term>` names one of `escapes` (closed vocabulary — extending it needs a decision record).  Meta ceilings are wide: an evolution ships the template tree and its meta twin in one PR. EVOL-047: runtime_surface is the POSITIVE list every deploying / release workflow asks before running its machinery (python3 scripts/gate.py runtime-surface --changed); always_deploy = hard exclusions that fire it regardless, each with its reason (workflow definitions; inputs a deployment-time gate reads); declared_reads = paths a deploying job reads outside the surface, each with its reason (parity exemptions). gate.py runtime-surface (a member of the gate profile, CI) holds the list to what the jobs and their scripts really read. The branch rule is untouched: every change ships via branch and pull request. deploying_workflows: the deploying / release-cutting workflow files the parity gate reads (globs).

always_deploy.reason: workflow definitions execute in CI/CD — a change here must run
input of the deployment-time gates (surface, profile)
the framework version and delivery mode the release reads

planning._doc: One planning stage (EVOL-048): a write to a governed path on a branch class with no framework planning phase needs an approved plan (python3 scripts/gate.py plan --path P; the PreToolUse hook check-plan-approval.sh asks it). governed_paths minus docs_exempt, except gate_inputs (documents a gate reads — governed like code). exempt_classes: the classes whose plan a framework phase owns; every other class is gated (fail-closed). plan_artefact: the branch's own plan artefact ({ID} = feature id) counts when its frontmatter status is approved. The approval marker is written only by the harness's plan approval (PostToolUse ExitPlanMode → gate.py plan --record); a marker approved on another branch is adopted once, within adoption_window_minutes. Framework repo: no class is exempt — an evolution branch has no framework phase; its ADR (status: accepted) is its plan, written first. In the framework repo every governed path is a gate input — the .md files under .claude/ and .context/templates/ ARE the product, never documentation; docs/ and README.md are the documentation.

agents._doc: EVOL-049: the two model FAMILIES as harness aliases (never pinned ids) — writers and critics on different families by construction (gate.py agents refuses equal aliases). The class policy, the roster and the per-spawn resolution live in the rule .context/templates/setup/rules/agents.md (a project: .claude/rules/agents.md).

documentation._doc: The ONE definition of a documentation path (EVOL-051): root-anchored globs in `paths`, minus `exclusions` (code whatever the extension). Read by python3 scripts/gate.py documentation — the push-gate preflight's review-lane skip, the planning gate's exemption (planning.docs_exempt is retired) and the seal's classification. A workflow or a behavioural contract (.claude/{instructions,skills,commands,hooks}) is never documentation.

verification._doc: One full verification loop per change (EVOL-051): `gates` is the path-to-gate map (what each full-loop gate READS, and the command that runs it — a command shared by two gates is executed once); `seal` is where python3 scripts/gate.py seal records a green loop per branch (untracked) and whether this repo owes one; `digest_artefacts` are the planning artefacts gate.py digests judges under docs/spec/{ID}/. The framework repo owes no local seal: its loop is the T2 suite CI runs on every pull request.

seal.reason: the framework repo's full loop is the T2 suite governance-check.yml runs on every pull request; no product build, no local seal
